## Schema of files generated by DMS in the Landing Bucket

The DMS Serverless is configured to replicate the `flight_radar` schema from Aurora PostgreSQL to the S3 bucket **`lakehouse-landing-<account_id>`** in **Parquet** (v2.0) format with **gzip** compression.

Each table generates its own set of Parquet files. Since `include_op_for_full_load = true`, the full load files include an additional `Op` column indicating the operation type (`I`, `U`, `D`).

### Columns per table (Parquet file)

#### `aircraft.parquet` — Aircraft registry
| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `icao24` | `VARCHAR(6)` | ICAO aircraft code (PK) |
| `registration` | `VARCHAR(20)` | Registration |
| `aircraft_type` | `VARCHAR(10)` | Type (e.g. B738, A320) |
| `manufacturer` | `VARCHAR(50)` | Manufacturer |
| `model` | `VARCHAR(50)` | Model |
| `serial_number` | `VARCHAR(30)` | Serial number |
| `operator_icao` | `VARCHAR(3)` | Operator ICAO code |
| `operator_name` | `VARCHAR(100)` | Operator name |
| `first_flight_date` | `DATE` | First flight date |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Creation date |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Update date |
| `dms_timestamp` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | DMS timestamp (full load) |
| `Op` | `CHAR(1)` | `I` (insert) — included via `include_op_for_full_load` |

#### `airports.parquet` — Airports
| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `icao_code` | `VARCHAR(4)` | ICAO code (PK) |
| `iata_code` | `VARCHAR(3)` | IATA code |
| `name` | `VARCHAR(200)` | Airport name |
| `city` | `VARCHAR(100)` | City |
| `country` | `VARCHAR(100)` | Country |
| `country_code` | `VARCHAR(2)` | Country code (ISO) |
| `latitude` | `DECIMAL(10,7)` | Latitude |
| `longitude` | `DECIMAL(10,7)` | Longitude |
| `elevation_ft` | `INTEGER` | Elevation in feet |
| `timezone` | `VARCHAR(50)` | Timezone |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Creation date |
| `dms_timestamp` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | DMS timestamp |
| `Op` | `CHAR(1)` | Operation |

#### `airlines.parquet` — Airlines
| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `icao_code` | `VARCHAR(3)` | ICAO code (PK) |
| `iata_code` | `VARCHAR(2)` | IATA code |
| `name` | `VARCHAR(200)` | Company name |
| `country` | `VARCHAR(100)` | Country |
| `callsign` | `VARCHAR(50)` | Callsign |
| `is_active` | `BOOLEAN` | Active? |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Creation date |
| `dms_timestamp` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | DMS timestamp |
| `Op` | `CHAR(1)` | Operation |

#### `flights.parquet` — Flights fact table
| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `flight_id` | `BIGINT` | Flight ID (PK) |
| `flight_number` | `VARCHAR(10)` | Flight number (e.g. AA1234) |
| `airline_icao` | `VARCHAR(3)` | FK → `airlines` |
| `aircraft_icao24` | `VARCHAR(6)` | FK → `aircraft` |
| `origin_airport` | `VARCHAR(4)` | FK → `airports` (origin) |
| `destination_airport` | `VARCHAR(4)` | FK → `airports` (destination) |
| `scheduled_departure` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Scheduled departure |
| `scheduled_arrival` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Scheduled arrival |
| `actual_departure` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Actual departure |
| `actual_arrival` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Actual arrival |
| `status` | `VARCHAR(20)` | Status (`scheduled`, `active`, `landed`, `cancelled`, `diverted`) |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Creation date |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Update date |
| `dms_timestamp` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | DMS timestamp |
| `Op` | `CHAR(1)` | Operation |

#### `aircraft_positions.parquet` — Positions (high volume, streaming)
| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `position_id` | `BIGINT` | Position ID (PK) |
| `aircraft_icao24` | `VARCHAR(6)` | FK → `aircraft` |
| `flight_id` | `BIGINT` | FK → `flights` |
| `latitude` | `DECIMAL(10,7)` | Latitude |
| `longitude` | `DECIMAL(10,7)` | Longitude |
| `altitude_ft` | `INTEGER` | Altitude in feet |
| `velocity_kts` | `DECIMAL(7,2)` | Velocity in knots |
| `heading` | `DECIMAL(5,2)` | Heading (degrees) |
| `vertical_rate_fpm` | `DECIMAL(7,2)` | Vertical rate (ft/min) |
| `on_ground` | `BOOLEAN` | On ground? |
| `recorded_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Capture time |
| `ingested_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Ingestion time |
| `dms_timestamp` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | DMS timestamp |
| `Op` | `CHAR(1)` | Operation |

#### `countries.parquet` — Countries
| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `BIGINT` | Country ID (PK) |
| `name` | `VARCHAR(100)` | Country name |
| `iso_code` | `VARCHAR(2)` | ISO country code |
| `iso_numeric` | `VARCHAR(3)` | ISO numeric code |
| `calling_code` | `VARCHAR(5)` | International calling code |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Creation date |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Update date |
| `dms_timestamp` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | DMS timestamp |
| `Op` | `CHAR(1)` | Operation |

#### `aircraft_types.parquet` — Aircraft types
| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `icao_code` | `VARCHAR(4)` | ICAO type code (PK) |
| `manufacturer` | `VARCHAR(50)` | Manufacturer |
| `model` | `VARCHAR(50)` | Model |
| `category` | `VARCHAR(30)` | Category |
| `engine_type` | `VARCHAR(30)` | Engine type |
| `engine_count` | `SMALLINT` | Number of engines |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Creation date |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Update date |
| `dms_timestamp` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | DMS timestamp |
| `Op` | `CHAR(1)` | Operation |

#### `routes.parquet` — Routes
| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `BIGINT` | Route ID (PK) |
| `airline_icao` | `VARCHAR(3)` | FK → `airlines` |
| `origin_airport` | `VARCHAR(4)` | FK → `airports` (origin) |
| `destination_airport` | `VARCHAR(4)` | FK → `airports` (destination) |
| `equipment` | `VARCHAR(20)` | Equipment (aircraft types) |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Creation date |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | Update date |
| `dms_timestamp` | `TIMESTAMPTZ` | DMS timestamp |
| `Op` | `CHAR(1)` | Operation |

### CDC Behavior (streaming)

CDC files are written to a dedicated prefix per table (e.g. `aircraft_cdc/`, `flights_cdc/`), produced by DMS via the `CdcPath` parameter. The streaming job reads only these CDC prefixes (`cdc_source_location`), leaving the full load folders untouched.

Files in the `cdc/` folder follow the same schema as the tables, with these differences:

- **`Op`** now records: `I` (insert), `U` (update), `D` (delete)
- Files are written with a maximum interval of **60 seconds** (`cdc_max_batch_interval`)
- The `dms_timestamp` column indicates when DMS captured the change
- `preserve_transactions = false` → each record is independent (no transactional grouping)

### Summary

The generate_dms_data.py populates exactly these 8 tables in the `flight_radar` schema of Aurora PostgreSQL, and DMS Serverless replicates everything to the landing bucket in **Parquet + gzip** format, partitioned by date (`YYYYMMDD`), with an `Op` column to track the operation type and `dms_timestamp` for the capture time.
